question.text: A trader buys 10 lots of USDINR 83.00 put at Rs. 0.15 premium. At expiry, USDINR is 82.40. Total profit?

explanation.text: The Logic: Long-put payoff per unit = max(83.00 - 82.40, 0) = 0.60. Net profit per unit after deducting premium = 0.60 - 0.15 = 0.45. With a currency-option lot size of 1000 units and 10 lots, total profit = 10 x 1000 x 0.45 = Rs. 4,500. The maximum possible loss for the buyer is the premium paid: 10 x 1000 x 0.15 = Rs. 1,500. The Trap: Rs. 6,000 uses the gross 0.60 payoff and forgets to subtract the premium; Rs. 1,500 is just the maximum-loss/premium figure rather than the realised profit. Note: Workbook reference — pp.84-85 (long-put payoff table and currency-option lot size of 1000 units).
